A_core_direct_lifespan.title: BMAL1-dependent regulation of the mTOR signaling pathway delays aging.
evidence_quotes: treatment with the mTORC1 inhibitor rapamycin increased lifespan of Bmal1−/− mice by 50%
we decided to compare activity of mTOR signaling in cells isolated from wild type and BMAL1-deficient mice

B_disease_model_survival.title: Long-term treatment of cancer-prone germline PTEN mutant mice with low-dose rapamycin extends lifespan and delays tumour development.
evidence_quotes: we administered a low dose of rapamycin from the age of 6 weeks onwards to mice with heterozygous germline Pten loss
Rapamycin was well tolerated and led to a highly significant improvement of survival in both male and female mice.

B_disease_model_survival.title: Acarbose suppresses symptoms of mitochondrial disease in a mouse model of Leigh syndrome.
evidence_quotes: Furthermore, rapamycin and acarbose have additive effects in delaying neurological symptoms and increasing maximum lifespan in Ndufs4 −/− mice.
Here we report the discovery that acarbose has comparable efficacy to rapamycin at delaying disease progression and increasing survival in Ndufs4 −/− mice.

C_secondary_contextual.title: Chemopreventive and chemotherapeutic actions of mTOR inhibitor in genetically defined head and neck squamous cell carcinoma mouse model.
C_secondary_contextual.venue: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
evidence_quotes: Tgfbr1 and Pten conditonal deletion (2cKO) mice were treated with Rapamycin before or after the onset of HNSCC, and the efficacy of this treatment was assessed by determining tumor burden, longevity, and molecular analysis of the mTOR pathway.
Chemopreventive Rapamycin treatment significantly delayed the onset of the HNSCC tumors and prolonged survival in 2cKO mice.
demote_reasons: no quote names a control term

C_secondary_contextual.title: Rapamycin doses sufficient to extend lifespan do not compromise muscle mitochondrial content or endurance.
evidence_quotes: we tested whether rapamycin, at the same doses used to extend lifespan, affects mitochondrial function in skeletal muscle.
rapamycin-treated mice had endurance equivalent to that of untreated controls, and isolated, permeabilized muscle fibers displayed similar rates of oxygen consumption.
